---
title: "Mixed graphs with multiple edges"
format: html
---

The adjacency matrix $G$ of a mixed graph $\mathcal{G}$ with node set $V$ and edge set $E$ is a $|V| \times |V|$ matrix defined as a sum of three different adjacency matrices   $G = A + B + L$  with elements  $A = (a_{ij})$, $B = (b_{ij})$ and $L = (l_{ij})$
defined as follows.

- The adjacency matrix of the arrows 
$$
a_{ij}  = \begin{cases}
          1 &     \iff i \rightarrow j \text{ in } \mathcal{G}\\
          0 &  \text{otherwise}\\
          \end{cases}
$$
- the adjacency matrix of the bi-directed arrows
  $$
  b_{ij}  = b_{ji} = \begin{cases}
          10 &     \iff i -\!\!- j \text{ in } \mathcal{G}\\
          0 &  \text{otherwise}\\
          \end{cases}
  $$
- The adjacency matrix of the undirected edges   
  $$
  w_{ij}  = w_{ji} = \begin{cases}
          100 &     \iff i \leftrightarrow j \text{ in } \mathcal{G}\\
          0 &  \text{otherwise}\\
          \end{cases}
  $$



The elements $G_{ij}$ for $i \ne j$ can take the following forms

$$
\small
\begin{array}{lll} 
         &  \text{Edges}            &  (G_{ij}, G_{ji})  & \text{edge type} \\ \hline  
         &   (1, 0)                       & (1, 0)    &  \text{right arrow}  \\ 
         &   (0,1)                        &  (0,1)     & \text{left arrow}  \\
         &  (10,10)                       & (10, 10)   &    \text{line} \\       
         &  (100,100)                     &  (100, 100) &    \text{arc}  \\
         & \text{Double edges}            &            &             \\           
         &  (0,1)+(1,0)                   & (1,1)      &    \text{two arrows}   \\        
         &  (10,10)+(0,1)                 & (10,11)    &    \text{line + arrow}\\       
         &  (10,10)+(100,100)             & (110,110)   &    \text{line + arc}      \\    
         &  (0,1)+(100,100)               & (100, 101)  &  \text{arrow+arc}     \\
         &   \text{Three edges}           &             &                            \\ 
         &  (0,1)+(100,100)+(10,10)       &(110, 111) & \text{arrow, arc, line}\\  
         &  (0,1)+(1,0)+(10,10)           & (11,11)   & \text{two arrows and a line} \\   
         &  (0,1)+(1,0)+(100,100)         & (101,101)   & \text{two arrows and an  arc} \\          & \text{Four edges}              &             &  \\ 
      &  (0,1)+(1,0)+(10,10)+(100,100) & (111,111)   & \text{two arrows an arc and a line} \\    \hline   
\end{array}
$$

### Examples

```{r} 
library(ggm)
A <- DG( `1` ~ `2`, `2` ~ `3`, `3` ~ 1)
```
